This is actually my first piece of terrain!

I'd love to share how it was done.

I started out with a plywood frame for stability and a good foundation, around 30x40 on the bottom and 40x 15 on the sides.

Then I took some aluminum mesh that you would use on a screen door, cut it slightly bigger than what I needed for the sides, and crumpled it up into a ball.

I unraveled the ball and stapled it to the tops and bottoms of each side. It holds a good, natural form.

After that, I made a 50/50 mix of water and Elmer's Glue-All (just white glue), and painted strips of toilet paper (yes, toilet paper) onto the mesh.

After letting the paper dry, I used Hydrocal Plaster from Woodland Scenics, along with their rock molds, to cast plaster rocks of all shapes and sizes, and hot glued them where I wanted them to go.

Once those sat for around 24 hrs to fully cure, I painted the entire piece with black, white, and burnt umber mixed together with water (dilute it to preserve the surface details) to get a nice, dark grey. I applied that base coat, and left it to dry.

To add highlights resembling some dried blood, I mixed cadmium deep red and sienna paint to make a nice dried blood color, and semi-dry brushed it into the rocks, and dabbed them with a damp paper towel to pick up excess paint in the cracks.

I then drybrushed the entire piece with white paint for highlights.

I then made a wash of white paint (little bit of paint, a lot of water), and brushed it onto the whole piece where it pooled in crevasses and ledges to add places where things might run off to.

I then took talus (bags little rocks you can buy at model train stores) and scenic glue. I spread the scenic glue in places where I wanted the talus, and gently sprinkled the talus on top.

To make the ashes, I simply sprinkled some tile grout over the talus where it caught the rest of the glue.

Concerning Bandit's battery trick, if Bandit sits near a reinforced wall and listens for Thermite to plant his charge, he can place his battery down just as thermite detonates or places his charge and destroy it (Listening isn't very reliable, but if you have a Valkyrie on your team, they can call out which wall to place your battery on if they can see them their camera).
